blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence by repairing automatic lantern audio causality, restoring readable authored-cemetery traversal and composition, and hardening dense-wave performance while implementing the required upgrade-choice visual hierarchy.

diagnosis.root_cause: The Warden Lantern authoritative attack chain completes, but product-owned Effects routing produces no audible source events. The preserved cemetery package is intact, yet camera and additive spatial bindings leave mausoleum geometry dominant and obscure the Warden during traversal.

stop_conditions: Stop after exactly three bounded task scopes have candidate implementations and focused self-checks.
Do not replace, split, hide, duplicate, reposition authored child meshes, or destructively edit the preserved AuthoredCemeteryPackage or retained weapon component assets.
Stop once candidate evidence is ready for host/tester recapture; formal verdicts and issue closure remain host-owned.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause strategy from prior transform tuning: preserve the single native authored environment and repair additive camera, anchor, collision, navigation, and boundary bindings; trace and correct the product audio adapter and lifecycle routing while preserving retained weapon sources; and profile dense-wave costs with bounded changes while replacing text-stacked upgrade choices with authored visual hierarchy.

code: Run native Godot syntax, scene/resource load, and static checks for all modified candidate files.
Verify target paths are candidate-relative and preserve the intact authored map instance and retained weapon component hierarchy.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime and Tester recapture fresh boot, ordinary movement replay across spawn→critical route→landmark→perimeter, dense-wave state, automatic SEMI/AUTO audio windows with attack/damage/death/reset telemetry, and level-up draft focus interactions.
Use candidate-bound runtime_state, scene3d/collision, logs, mixed-output audio, frame-time counters, and upgrade-draft interaction artifacts; Tester owns pass/fail and issue closure.
visual: Capture shipped gameplay camera at spawn, critical route, central landmark/Warden encounter, and perimeter to verify external depth, readable Warden silhouette, stable landmark visibility, collision-aligned traversal, and no disappearance or occlusion drift.

Capture adjacent SEMI and quick AUTO attack frames paired with distinct runtime states, plus the level-up draft at keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states, verifying silhouettes/icons, truthful current-to-new deltas, visual hierarchy, and HUD readability.

done_when: The shipped gameplay camera presents the player and Warden together without mausoleum-dominant occlusion; the central landmark remains visible and the Warden silhouette is readable at ordinary movement distance.
Spawn, objective anchors, collision, navigation, and perimeter boundary align with native authored streets and terrain; no proxy floor or duplicate world fill is introduced.
Movement replay across spawn, critical route, cardinal landmark, and perimeter shows no pass-through, disappearance, or occlusion drift, and the authored package remains one intact runtime instance.
Tester can directly black-box verify traversal and white-box inspect camera, collision, boundary, and anchor bindings.
tasks.instructions: Repair the preserved AuthoredCemeteryPackage integration as a spatial/composition task. Adjust only additive camera framing, spawn/objective anchors, collision layers/shapes, navigation, and outer boundary bindings around the native streets, buildings, props, and landmark sightlines; remove or minimize unrelated proxy/support clutter. Explicitly demonstrate expand or larger traversable scale, external world or external depth, central building or landmark, collision, disappearance or occlusion, boundary or perimeter, and ordinary movement or movement replay. Keep native map hierarchy, materials, and meshes intact.
tasks.title: Rebase authored cemetery framing, traversal, and boundaries

done_when: One SEMI click and one quick AUTO tap each produce exactly one short, recognizable firearm transient in mixed output on the Effects bus, with no long ringing material-impact cue masking the report.
Automatic combat telemetry remains causally ordered attack→impact→damage→death/recovery; sustained AUTO starts only after cadence-valid continuation and stops on release and lifecycle reset.
Character-hit and enemy spatial cues remain separate from the player firearm report; compact impact VFX remain present if player world-surface impact audio is disabled.
Tester has direct same-session black-box audio capture and white-box routing/source checks for the repaired adapter.
tasks.instructions: Trace the product-owned Warden Lantern path from input cadence through attack, legal hit, damage, death, and recovery. Repair adapter, Effects-bus routing, envelope, gain, source selection, and lifecycle reset so SEMI and quick AUTO taps yield one bounded recognizable transient each. Preserve the retained component FireAudio/AutoFireAudio path and weapon identity; generic shot VFX must not replay the retained player recording. Keep character-hit and enemy spatial cues separate. If authored material tags cannot produce a short surface cue, disable player world-surface impact audio while preserving impact VFX and character-hit feedback. Verify pause, retry, release, and lifecycle reset.
tasks.title: Restore automatic lantern firearm report and causal audio chain

done_when: A dense-wave replay reaches the target high-enemy-count state without frame-time spikes beyond the existing release budget, runaway allocations, or accumulating timers/signals.
Enemy spawn, movement, damage, death, XP, and wave-director behavior remain functionally unchanged under profiled load; boss and wave transitions still occur and no new runtime errors appear.

Replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices with an authored visual hierarchy led by weapon or upgrade silhouettes/icons, followed by compact stat icons and truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas.

Choices never show NEW or LOCKED as a placeholder in the CURRENT value column, omit unchanged or exhaustive rows, use restrained copy, and expose complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus, hover, unavailable, and selected states.
Diagnostics identify the dominant dense-run cost and are disabled or release-gated; Tester can compare before/after frame time, enemy count, lifecycle telemetry, and the upgrade-draft presentation.
tasks.instructions: Profile the existing survivor-like dense wave and apply bounded, reversible optimization to the dominant candidate-side cost (pool/reuse, signal or timer cleanup, staggered updates, or readability-preserving culling as justified by measurements). Keep authoritative combat, XP, and wave-director semantics intact and gate diagnostics from release presentation. Implement survivor.choice_visual_hierarchy in the upgrade-draft surface: replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices with silhouettes/icons, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values limited to three decision-relevant stat deltas, no NEW or LOCKED CURRENT placeholders, no unchanged or exhaustive rows, restrained copy, visual hierarchy, and complete keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states. Provide deterministic dense and level-up replay setups for direct retest.
tasks.title: Harden dense waves and replace text-stacked upgrade choices
